title: Declaring It Is In The Best Interest of The OUSD to Piggyback On and Enter Into A Contract with CDW Government, LLC, Properly Entered into Through CalSave/Monterey County Office of Education (MCOE) - OUSD Purchase Agreement -Technology Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education (Board) of Resolution No. 2526-0152 - Declaring It Is In The Best Interest of The District to Piggyback On and Enter Into A Contract with CDW Government, LLC, Properly Entered into Through CalSave/Monterey County Office of Education (MCOE), CalSAVE Bid No. 538902 awarded to CDW-Government and Approval by the Board of an E-Rate Cybersecurity Pilot Program Purchase Agreement (Contract Number 146545, Spin No. 143005588, FCC Registration No. 0012123287) by and between the District and CDW Government, LLC, Vernon Hills, IL, for Cybersecurity Services and Support, as specified in Agreement, for the term September 16, 2025 to September 15, 2028, in a not-to exceed amount of $1,509,895.00, subject to award of E-Rate funding.
headline: Buys $1.51M of cybersecurity services from CDW Government through 2028 via another agency's bid
summary: The district would pay CDW Government, LLC up to $1,509,895 over three years for cybersecurity services and support, under a federal E-Rate pilot program for school cybersecurity. The district is buying through an existing bid held by the Monterey County Office of Education instead of running its own bid. The purchase depends on the district being awarded E-Rate funding.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – NG Builder Company – Emerson Elementary School Site Improvements Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of an Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Nicholas Guiterrez dba NG Builder Company, Santa Clara, CA, for the latter to demolish existing play structures, safety surfacing, basketball hoop poles, enhance the garden space, and prep surface to receive new nature area; install safety surfacing tiles and drainage systems for new play structures;* prepare walls for murals, tree planting with irrigation and drainage, and seal coating of existing pavement, as part of the Emerson Elementary School Site Improvements Project, in the amount of $397,666.00, which includes a contingency fee of $48,000.00, as the lowest responsive bidder, with the work anticipated to commence on September 29, 2025, and required to be completed within sixty-six days (66), with an anticipated ending of December 4, 2025.
____
*Furnishing and installation of new play structure is by Others.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Hires NG Builder Company for $397,666 to upgrade the Emerson Elementary play area and garden
summary: The district would pay NG Builder Company $397,666, including a $48,000 contingency, to tear out old play structures and surfacing, add safety surfacing and drainage, prepare walls for murals, plant trees and reseal pavement at Emerson Elementary School. The company was the lowest responsive bidder. Work is expected to run from September 29 to December 4, 2025; the new play structure itself is provided by others.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Redgwick Construction Company – Madison Primary School Site Improvement Project – Department of Buildings & Grounds
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor, by and between the District and Redgwick Construction Company, Oakland, CA, for the latter’s installation of additional base rock, and over-excavation in selected locations to ensure proper paving preparation, addressing unforeseen conditions encountered during asphalt removal and replacement in several areas where subgrade conditions did not meet compacting requirements, as detailed in PCO No. 1, for the Madison Primary School Site Improvement Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $30,256.01, increasing the Agreement amount from $1,347,100.00 to $1,377,356.01. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $30,256.01 to Redgwick's Madison Primary paving contract for unforeseen ground conditions
summary: This change order adds up to $30,256.01 to Redgwick Construction Company's contract at Madison Primary School, raising it from $1,347,100.00 to $1,377,356.01. The extra base rock and digging were needed because soil under the old asphalt did not meet compaction requirements. The change order is based on a preliminary change order (PCO No. 1); all other contract terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Medical Business Professional Services Group, Inc. - Risk Management Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Medical Business Professional Services Group, Inc, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide diagnostic checks of Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) that are placed in administrative buildings and on campuses throughout District, replace AED batteries, replace expiring adult and child AED pads, maintain accessory emergency medical supplies; update labor law posters and provide District Health Services with a physician for prescriptions services (i.e., Epi-Pens), medical oversight and consultations as needed, via Risk Management Department, for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $99,000.00.

vendor_name: Medical Business Professional Services Group, Inc.

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Nadja Conway - Talent / Human Resources Department

title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - Peer Forward – High School Linked Learning Office
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement (NCSA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) by and between the District and Peer Forward, Washington, DC, for the latter, under the NCSA, to provide its Educator Training/Advisor Coaching, initially a 4-day residential workshop held on a college campus where the educators (or advisors) working with the peer leaders selected by the school to receive training and professional development on how to engage their Peer Leaders and effectively utilize their Advisor Playbook, resources, and materials, as further described - School Year Implementation, Data and Evaluation, Digital Curriculum, Work-Based Learning,  in Exhibit A of the Agreement incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for participating OUSD schools: Castlemont High School, Fremont High School, Madison Park Academy, and Oakland Technical High School, for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, and under the Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), the terms and conditions of the District's transmission of or sharing of pupil data with Peer Forward and the protection by Peer Forward of such data for the same term as the NCSA.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost Peer Forward training and data-sharing deal for four high schools
summary: Peer Forward would train and coach educators at four schools, starting with a four-day residential workshop, so they can lead peer leaders, at no cost to the district. A separate data sharing agreement (DSA) sets the rules for sharing student data with Peer Forward and protecting it. Both run July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, and the start date was before this approval.
schools: Castlemont High School; Fremont High School; Madison Park Academy; Oakland Technical High School
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

schools: East Oakland Pride; Elmhurst Middle School; Frick United Academy of Language; Castlemont High School; OUSD Student Welcome Center

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Bay Area Community Resources - Community Schools and Student Services Department

headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $22,500 for an AmeriCorps member to help students in unstable housing

The member would help with daily check-ins, social-emotional learning groups, attendance, family outreach and enrollment over 36 weeks.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement - Terraphase Engineering, Inc. - Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Terraphase Engineering, Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to collect a total of twelve soil samples from the four proposed boring locations (up to three samples per borings) to be advanced by the geotechnical engineering contractor, in coordination with the ongoing Environmental Site Assessment at the site, as outlined in the Proposal dated July 16, 2025, which is attached to Exhibit A of the Agreement, for the Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project, in an additional amount of $9,131.00, which includes a contingency fee of $830.00, increasing the amount of the Agreement from $10,670.00 to $19,801.00, and extending the term of the Agreement from May 15, 2025 through December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026, (an additional 181 calendar days). All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $9,131 for Terraphase soil sampling at Garfield Elementary and extends its term
summary: This amendment adds money and time to Terraphase Engineering's agreement to collect twelve soil samples from four proposed boring locations at Garfield Elementary School, alongside an ongoing environmental site assessment. The total rises from $10,670 to $19,801, and the end date moves from December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
